asked_at: Paytm (reported on The Product Folks case library)
round_and_level: PM round, analytical RCA; APM campus to PM [uncertain]
difficulty: Medium-Hard - the drop has a dominant external, regulatory cause (RBI action on Paytm Payments Bank), but the candidate has to show how it travelled through product dependencies (wallet, FASTag, @paytm UPI handles, NPCI onboarding freeze) rather than just saying 'RBI ban'
market_and_industry: India; fintech / UPI payments super-app (consumer payments, merchant QR and soundbox, lending distribution). Mass-market and Bharat users, Hindi-first, budget Android phones; strong in Tier-2/3 merchants
exact_prompt: Paytm's monthly active users are down 25%. What happened?
source_and_verification: Reported. The Product Folks lists 'Paytm's monthly active user count has decreased by 25%' as an RCA case (https://www.theproductfolks.com/product-management-case-studies/paytms-monthly-active-user-count-has-decreased); also covered as a YouTube RCA walkthrough (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OU433YcZJm0). Year reported about 2024 [uncertain]. The 25% figure closely matches a real event: Paytm's MTU fell from 10.4 crore (Jan 2024) to 7.8 crore (Jun 2024), about -25%, after RBI restrictions on Paytm Payments Bank (https://inc42.com/buzz/paytm-q1-highlights-loss-widens-but-co-expects-revenue-to-improve-in-coming-quarters). The case is solved as that real event; the exhibit splits are illustrative.
context_as_of: As of Nov 2026: Paytm reported Q2 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) MTU of 8.5 crore, up 1 crore YoY, its biggest annual addition in about 3 years. PAT was Rs 225 crore (about 10.7x YoY), revenue Rs 2,648 crore (+28%), GMV Rs 7.1 lakh crore (+26%) and merchant subscriptions 1.64 crore (https://paytm.com/document/ir/financial-results/fy2026-27/Paytm-Q2-FY27-Earnings-Release-USD.pdf ; https://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/279399152/paytm-q2-fy27-profit-rises-over-10-fold-to-225-crore-revenue-grows-28-to-2648-crore). Q1 FY27 MTU was 8.0 crore (average), and Paytm defines MTU as unique users who completed a transaction on the Paytm app or Paytm for Business app in a calendar month (https://paytm.com/document/ir/financial-results/Paytm_Earning-Release_Q1-FY-2027.pdf). So MTU is still below the Jan 2024 peak of 10.4 crore. UPI market share (by volume, May 2026): PhonePe 46.26%, Google Pay 32.75%, Paytm 7.9% (up from 6.8% in May 2025). PhonePe plus Google Pay fell below 80% for the first time (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/economy-and-policy/phonepe-google-pay-combined-upi-market-share-drops-below-80-for-first-time). History used in the case: on 31 Jan 2024 RBI barred Paytm Payments Bank (PPBL) from taking deposits, wallet top-ups and FASTag top-ups after 29 Feb 2024 (extended to 15 Mar 2024). NPCI then approved Paytm as a third-party app provider with Axis, HDFC, SBI and Yes Bank as PSP banks to migrate @paytm handles, but barred onboarding of new UPI users until Oct 2024 [uncertain on exact dates]. Stale-risk flag: the 'MAU' in the prompt is MTU in Paytm's own reporting.
regulatory_context: Material and central. (1) RBI Section 35A action on Paytm Payments Bank (31 Jan 2024): no fresh deposits, credits, wallet or FASTag top-ups or NCMC top-ups after 15 Mar 2024, for persistent non-compliance including KYC. (2) NPCI third-party app provider (TPAP) approval for One97 (Mar 2024), with migration of @paytm UPI handles to four PSP banks, and a ban on onboarding new UPI users until NPCI lifted it in Oct 2024 [uncertain on exact date]. (3) NHAI / IHMCL dropped Paytm FASTag from authorised issuers, forcing users to buy new FASTags. (4) NPCI's proposed 30% per-app UPI volume cap, with the deadline now reported as 31 Dec 2026; status not final (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/economy-and-policy/phonepe-google-pay-combined-upi-market-share-drops-below-80-for-first-time). It would benefit Paytm as the #3 app. (5) Zero MDR on UPI P2M, which limits monetisation of recovered users. RBI digital-lending guidelines constrain how fast lending can be used to win users back.
public_data_anchors: 1) Paytm MTU 10.4 crore in Jan 2024, 8.9 crore in Mar 2024, 7.8 crore in Jun 2024 (https://inc42.com/buzz/paytm-q1-highlights-loss-widens-but-co-expects-revenue-to-improve-in-coming-quarters ; https://businessinsider.in/stock-market/news/paytm-q1fy25-results-revenue-from-payment-services-jumps-to-rs-900-crore-monthly-transacting-users-in-june-dip-to-7-8-crore/articleshow/111853802.cms). 2) Q1 FY25 revenue down 36% YoY to Rs 1,502 crore, net loss Rs 840 crore (Inc42, Jul 2024). 3) Q1 FY27 MTU 8.0 crore average, merchant transactions 1,669 crore (Paytm earnings release, Jul 2026). 4) Q2 FY27 MTU 8.5 crore, PAT Rs 225 crore, GMV Rs 7.1 lakh crore, merchant subscriptions 1.64 crore (Paytm, Oct-Nov 2026). 5) UPI share May 2026: PhonePe 46.26%, Google Pay 32.75%, Paytm 7.9% (Outlook Business). 6) UPI processed 21,860 crore transactions in FY26 (https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/upi-processes-21860-crore-transactions-in-fy26-peak-growth-seen-in-dec-jan-months-523412-2026-03-31). 7) UPI crossed 23 bn transactions in May 2026 (https://inc42.com/buzz/upi-transactions-jump-3-8-mom-in-may-cross-23-bn-mark/).
framework_applied: RCA framework (frameworks.md section 4). Step 1 Clarify - metric: 'MAU' is Paytm's MTU (unique users completing at least one transaction in a calendar month on the Paytm or Paytm for Business app); time frame: Jan to Jun 2024, a sharp fall from Feb with a cliff after 15 Mar; scope: -25% (10.4 to 7.8 crore), all regions, worst in wallet-, FASTag- and PPBL-linked users. Step 2a Data: MTU definition unchanged, events firing; the drop also shows in GMV and app opens, so it's real. Step 2b Internal: transaction funnel by use case (wallet, PPBL UPI, other-bank UPI, recharge/bills, FASTag, tickets) shows losses concentrated in PPBL-dependent flows; product changes such as forced @paytm handle migration and paused cashback amplified it. Step 2c External: RBI action on PPBL (regulation), NPCI new-user onboarding freeze, NHAI de-listing Paytm FASTag, a media trust shock, and competitors (PhonePe, Google Pay) poaching merchants and users; seasonality in the ticketing business is a minor factor. Step 2d Behaviour: users multi-home on UPI, so switching cost is close to zero once trust breaks. Step 3 Hypothesise-test with wide questions (is it real? which use case? new vs existing users? consumer vs merchant?). Step 4 Land: a regulatory shock on the banking partner broke three product rails and froze acquisition; validate with cohort retention by PPBL dependency and with new-user adds; fix with migration UX, trust messaging and merchant-led win-back.

clarifying_questions.q: Is 'MAU' app opens, or transacting users? Paytm reports MTU.
clarifying_questions.a: Use MTU: unique users with at least one successful transaction in the month on the Paytm or Paytm for Business app.

clarifying_questions.q: Over what period, and was it sudden?
clarifying_questions.a: From 10.4 crore in January to 7.8 crore in June. It started falling in February and dropped hard after mid-March.

clarifying_questions.q: Is the drop the same across consumer and merchant users?
clarifying_questions.a: Both fell. Consumers fell more in absolute terms; merchants also churned, mainly soundbox and QR users.

clarifying_questions.q: Is it across all geographies and platforms?
clarifying_questions.a: Broadly national, on both Android and iOS. Slightly worse in Tier-1 metros, where users depended more on wallet and FASTag.

clarifying_questions.q: Did anything happen to Paytm or its partners recently - product, regulatory, banking?
clarifying_questions.a: You tell me. What would you check first?

clarifying_questions.q: Are new-user additions and existing-user retention both down, or just one?
clarifying_questions.a: Both. New UPI user additions are close to zero for a few months.

clarifying_questions.q: Is GMV and app traffic also down, or just transacting users?
clarifying_questions.a: GMV and app opens are also down, but GMV less than users, because heavy merchant-payment users stayed.

clarifying_questions.q: Has overall UPI in India grown over the same period?
clarifying_questions.a: Yes, UPI kept growing month on month. PhonePe and Google Pay gained share.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Paytm's MAU is down 25%. What happened?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Let me clarify the metric, timing and scope, then work through data, internal, external and behaviour causes. Paytm reports monthly transacting users, not app opens. Is that the metric?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Yes, MTU: a successful transaction in the month on Paytm or Paytm for Business.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Over what period, and was it sudden or gradual?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: 10.4 crore in January to 7.8 crore in June. It started falling in February and dropped hard after mid-March. Exhibit 1.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text:
A cliff with a date on it usually means a release, a policy or a partner change. India-wide UPI kept growing, so this isn't the category shrinking; it's Paytm losing share. Here's my board:

MTU -25%
|- 1. Data: definition change, tracking break
|- 2. Internal: funnel by use case (wallet, UPI, bills, FASTag, tickets); releases; cashback cuts; merchant churn
|- 3. External: RBI/NPCI action, banking partner, competitors, media/trust, seasonality
|- 4. Behaviour: multi-homing, trust, habit moving to PhonePe/GPay

First, data. Did GMV and app traffic drop too?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Both down, GMV less than users. No definition change.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: So it's real. GMV falling less than users suggests light users left and heavy merchant-payment users stayed. Wide question: was this new users not arriving, existing users leaving, or both?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 3. Both. New additions fell from 45 lakh to almost nothing, and existing-user churn more than doubled in March.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Acquisition going to near zero for months isn't normal product decay. It points to a block on onboarding. Combined with a mid-March cliff, my lead hypothesis is external and regulatory: something hit Paytm Payments Bank, the bank behind the wallet, FASTag and @paytm UPI handles. Was there regulatory action?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Yes. On 31 January RBI barred PPBL from deposits and wallet or FASTag top-ups, effective mid-March. What does that do to MTU?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: It breaks three rails at once. Wallet users can't add money. FASTag users must buy a new tag from another bank. @paytm UPI handles have to move to partner banks. And if NPCI paused new UPI user onboarding, the top of the funnel stops too. I'd confirm with a split by each user's main rail in January.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 2.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That confirms it. Wallet users kept only 45%, FASTag users 40%, and @paytm handle users 70%, while users on other-bank UPI kept 92%. Roughly 70% of the loss is on PPBL-dependent rails. Users not tied to PPBL were barely affected, which is my control group.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: But the other-bank UPI users weren't affected by RBI at all, and they still lost 8%. Why?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: That's the trust spillover, the behaviour bucket. Headlines said 'Paytm banned'. Many people couldn't tell the bank from the app, and UPI has close to zero switching cost, since PhonePe and GPay were already on their phones. Can I see the migration funnel for @paytm users?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 4. 62% started migration, 48% completed, 41% transacted again. Top reason for dropping off: they thought Paytm was shut down.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: So the product amplified the shock: a migration flow with OTP failures and messaging that didn't say clearly 'Paytm app works, only the bank changed'. That's a fixable internal cause on top of the external one. What about the merchant side?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Exhibit 5. Merchants with PPBL settlement had to switch banks; soundbox base fell about 10%, and rivals offered free devices.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Merchant churn hurts twice. Those merchants drop out of MTU themselves, and consumers see fewer Paytm QRs at the kirana, which weakens the habit. Last, minor factors: seasonality in ticketing or a cashback pull-back?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: Ticketing had a seasonal dip, under 2% of MTU. Cashback was trimmed to save cost.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Then here's my landing. Root cause: a regulatory shock to the banking partner. RBI's action on PPBL broke the wallet, FASTag and @paytm UPI rails, and an NPCI onboarding freeze took new-user adds to near zero. Ranked: (1) PPBL rail breakage, about 60-70% of the loss; (2) a trust spillover onto users who weren't affected, made worse by a leaky migration flow and confusing messaging, about 20-25%; (3) merchant churn and cashback cuts, with seasonality last. To validate: retention by January rail (done), new-user adds against the NPCI freeze dates, and a difference-in-differences test with PhonePe and GPay share gains in the same months. Fix: one-tap guided handle migration with OTP retries; a loud 'Paytm is working' trust campaign in vernacular and in-app; a push to merchants to switch settlement banks, with free soundbox retention offers; and FASTag win-back via partner-bank tags. For when NPCI lifts the freeze, prepare referral and cashback-led re-acquisition. Long term: never run a core rail through a single bank again; keep a multi-bank PSP setup.

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Interviewer
solution_walkthrough.text: It's now Nov 2026. Paytm is back at 8.5 crore MTU. Is the problem solved?

solution_walkthrough.speaker: Candidate
solution_walkthrough.text: Partly. It's growing again: +1 crore YoY and UPI share up from 6.8% to 7.9%. But it's still about 2 crore below the January 2024 peak. The 30% UPI cap, if it is enforced by end-2026, is the next tailwind. I'd focus on getting the dormant ex-wallet users back with credit-on-UPI and bill-pay hooks, not just cashback.

answer_and_recommendation: Ranked causes: (1) RBI's restrictions on Paytm Payments Bank (31 Jan 2024, effective 15 Mar 2024) broke the wallet, FASTag and @paytm UPI rails, and NPCI froze new-UPI-user onboarding, which cut both retention and acquisition. This is about 60-70% of the 25% drop (MTU 10.4 to 7.8 crore, real). (2) A trust spillover and a leaky handle-migration flow pushed even unaffected users to PhonePe and Google Pay, which cost nothing to switch to (illustrative share about 20-25%). (3) Merchant settlement churn plus cashback cuts weakened the habit; ticketing seasonality was minor. Recommendation: fix the migration UX (one-tap, OTP retries, clear status), run a vernacular trust campaign ('the app works; only the bank changed'), do merchant retention with free soundbox and fast settlement-bank switching, offer FASTag replacement, and prepare a re-acquisition push for when onboarding reopens; structurally, run on multiple PSP banks. Risks: cashback-led win-back attracts low-quality users and burns cash (mitigate with targeted offers to lapsed high-value users), and further regulatory scrutiny (mitigate with compliance-first KYC). Closing line: 'Paytm didn't lose users because the product got worse. It lost them because its bank went down and took three payment rails and new-user onboarding with it. The trust gap afterwards turned a 15% hit into 25%, and that part is ours to fix.'
counter_metrics_guardrails: Guardrails: GMV per MTU and merchant-payment share (so win-back isn't empty cashback churn); cost per reactivated user and contribution margin; payment success rate and migration OTP failure rate; KYC compliance and fraud or chargeback rate (aggressive re-onboarding must not repeat PPBL's KYC failures); merchant soundbox active base and settlement time; customer complaints to RBI Ombudsman and NPCI. Counter-metric: UPI market share against PhonePe and GPay, so that MTU growth just from UPI category growth isn't mistaken for recovery.

follow_up_twists.twist: Suppose there was no regulatory action, and the drop happened anyway in the same months.
follow_up_twists.response: Then I'd look for a share shift. Check PhonePe/GPay cashback campaigns, a Paytm cashback cut, and UPI Lite/credit-on-UPI features rivals launched; and split by cohort to see whether lapsed users moved to a rival via UPI intent data from merchants.

follow_up_twists.twist: Leadership wants to spend Rs 500 crore on cashback to win back users. Do you agree?
follow_up_twists.response: Only targeted. Spend on lapsed users who were high-frequency merchant payers or bill payers, measured by 90-day retained GMV per rupee, not blanket cashback to people who will churn the day it ends.

follow_up_twists.twist: What if only merchant MTU dropped, not consumers?
follow_up_twists.response: Then I'd look at settlement banking, soundbox rental pricing, MDR or device-fee changes and competitor field-force offers, and segment by merchant tier and city.

common_pitfalls: 1) Saying 'RBI banned Paytm' and stopping. The interviewer wants the mechanism: which rails broke, why new users stopped coming, and why unaffected users also left. 2) Treating it as a UX or app-bug problem, and proposing redesigns while ignoring the dated regulatory cliff. 3) Confusing Paytm (One97, the app) with Paytm Payments Bank (an associate entity). The UPI app kept working through partner PSP banks. 4) Ignoring the merchant side, which feeds consumer habit through QR codes and soundboxes at local shops.
skills_tested: structuring, business sense, quant, prioritisation, communication, empathy, execution
